name: DigiCo ADL1 (ex-YourDC Edinburgh Parks DC1)

address.note: OSM building 'DigiCo ADL1, 23-27 Woomera Avenue' (source 7); datacentermap lists 23 Woomera Avenue; PeeringDB gives 'Woomera Avenue, Edinburgh Parks 5111'. Edinburgh Parks estate, City of Salisbury

lat.note: Geocoded 2026-09-27: OpenStreetMap Nominatim building 'DigiCo ADL1, 23-27 Woomera Avenue' (-34.7404086, 138.6440232); ArcGIS World Geocoder gives the same point for 23 Woomera Ave (PointAddress, score 100). PeeringDB point (-34.7328, 138.6362) is about 1 km off and not used.

builder.note: not found. Contractors named: Contracting Site Solutions (CSS, contracting/specialist technology services, source 5) and Airmaster (mechanical services and BMS, source 6); no head contractor identified

developer.note: founded by Scott Hicks and Greg Siegele; later acquired via iseek by DigiCo (HMC Capital) 2024

mw_it.note: DigiCo ADL1 page (search snippet): 'tier III specification with 1.2MW of Installed IT Capacity', ~2,280 m2 NLA on 22,920 sqm land. The widely quoted '8 MW' (iTnews, datacentermap) is power supply: four 2 MW transformers, dual substations (source 1). Planned 15 MW expansion is a separate excluded item (list/excluded.csv 'ADL1 expansion'); datacentermap now lists 15 MW

mw_grid.note: iTnews: '8 MW power' via four 2 MW transformers and dual substations; standby 2 x 1.1 MVA diesel generators (sources 1, 3)

cost_aud_m.note: iTnews: '$30 million' data centre (includes purchase/conversion of an existing 6,000 m2 building on a 25,000 m2 site)

authority.note: not found; site is in the City of Salisbury (SA Development Act 1993 applied in 2015)

jobs_construction_other.note: web-search summary (source 8, not read in full): 'YourDC created 100 jobs for the construction of the facility'; original wording and definition not seen

construction_start.note: search snippet of DCD (source 8): YourDC 'established in 2015' and 'promptly started building the Edinburgh Parks facility at a former Tenneco Walker car exhaust factory'; month not found

construction_end.note: iTnews: facility opened 26 May 2016 with 200 of 800 racks built; four expansion stages planned over two years (source 1); CSS launch post dated 25 May 2016 (source 5)

open_questions: scope: excluded (decision 2026-09-27) - installed IT capacity 1.2 MW (DigiCo) is below the 5 MW floor; the '8 MW' figure is transformer/grid supply; removed from master.csv and listed in excluded.csv. Revisit if the 15 MW expansion is built
conversion of an existing factory building, not a new build
